name: s3-protrusions-to-enclosure
title: S3 — Protrusions to enclosure: can protrusion mechanics reach stable wrapping?
concept: Compartmentalization made operational as the topology and energy of enclosing membranes. A host protrusion of finite membrane area extends at an observed rate and attempts to wrap a bacterial partner; enclosure succeeds, per partner radius, only when the available area covers the partner AND adhesion clears the Helfrich bending cost. Classical engulfment, inside-out wrapping, and a no-enclosure control are compared over a partner-radius ensemble.
question: Can observed archaeal protrusion mechanics plausibly transition from contact to stable wrapping / engulfment, within membrane area, bending-cost, and timescale budgets? Morphology alone cannot demonstrate engulfment.
hypothesis: Under cryo-ET-constrained bending moduli and adhesion, at least one topology (classical engulfment or inside-out wrapping) reaches a stable enclosed state over a realistic partner-size range with conserved membrane area, while a no-enclosure or weak-adhesion control does not.
claim: Physical enclosure is a separate hurdle from metabolic benefit (S1/S2): observed protrusion mechanics can, under favorable area and adhesion budgets, reach stable wrapping over a majority of the partner-size range — but a beneficial symbiosis need not imply ingestive ability, and enclosure fails without wrapping (no-enclosure) or when adhesion cannot pay the bending cost.

behavior_tests.name: enclosure-geometrically-feasible
behavior_tests.description: At least one topology reaches stable enclosure for a majority of the partner-size ensemble (enclosure probability > 0.5). The threshold discriminates the wrapping topologies from the no-enclosure and weak-adhesion controls.

provenance.note: Calibrated (classical engulfment, protrusion_area=4 um^2, adhesion=600 kT, kappa=20 kT, 30 steps): enclosure_probability settles to 0.61 (PASS; inside-out wrapping reaches 0.98). Two failure routes read 0.0: the no-enclosure control and the weak-adhesion control (adhesion below the 8*pi*kappa bending cost).

behavior_tests.name: membrane-area-conserved
behavior_tests.description: Membrane area is conserved through the deformation (no area created from nothing).

provenance.note: Area conservation under bending (residual ~0 by construction).

findings.statement: Enclosure is topology-gated, not a settled yes. The higher-fidelity active-protrusion membrane-wrapping model (Helfrich bending + adhesion + tension + finite protrusion area + active force F*R, 3D; the mechanism the question is about) supersedes the coarser arms: classical EXTERNAL engulfment reaches a stable wrap for only a MINORITY of partners (probability 0.27, a narrow 0.41-0.56 um window), with the active protrusion load-bearing (raises it from 0.17; 36% of enclosures need the force); INSIDE-OUT invagination (Baum & Baum) is far more feasible (0.83). The coarse arms overstated it — the 2D passive-adhesion CPM read 1.00 (but that is regime-assumed, J_hs < J_sM-J_hM, with no protrusion) and the static area+bending budget read 0.61/0.98. So whether the enclosure hypothesis is supported depends on which topology is primary, which remains an open investigation decision. Enclosure is a separate hurdle from metabolic benefit; morphology alone does not demonstrate engulfment.

superseded.reason: wrong mechanism for the posed question (no active protrusion; 2D; engulfment assumed by the chosen adhesion hierarchy)

provenance.note: Active-protrusion membrane-wrapping model (viva_genesis.composites.protrusion_enclosure_membrane, MembraneWrappingProcess; continuum energetics validated against the reduced-adhesion=2 wrapping threshold) over the 0.2-0.8 um partner-radius ensemble at grounded parameters (kappa 20 kT, adhesion 250 kT/um^2, tension 200 kT/um^2, protrusion force 10 pN, A_max 4 um^2): classical engulfment enclosure probability 0.27 (window 0.41-0.56 um; protrusion required for 36%); inside-out 0.83. Companions (lower fidelity): CPM spatial arm 1.00 (regime-assumed), area+bending budget 0.61/0.98. Next fidelity rung: a triangulated-mesh run (pbg-mem3dg).

literature_anchors.expectation: Cryo-ET constrains Asgard membrane morphology and actin-based structure.

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: New first-fidelity model built for S3 (no existing composite fit). enclosure_probability over a partner-radius ensemble is the feasibility gate; membrane area is conserved by construction. The full deformable-membrane PDE with explicit protrusion dynamics is the next-fidelity arm.

baseline.name: cpm-spatial
baseline.note: Spatial companion (campaign composite B) — the real Rust Cellular Potts engine with actual boundaries. Enclosure is an emergent, measured outcome (host coverage of the symbiont boundary), not an area/bending threshold; the wrapping transition tracks j_hs = j_sM - j_hM. Measured j_hs=6 (strong adhesion) -> enclosure_fraction 1.000; j_hs=18 (weak) -> 0.176.

baseline.name: membrane-wrapping
baseline.note: Higher-fidelity continuum-energetics arm — the membrane-wrapping transition (Deserno/Lipowsky) with an active protrusion force, the mechanism the question is about (not passive differential adhesion). Classical external engulfment reaches enclosure only in a narrow size window (0.41-0.56 um), for a minority of partners (probability 0.27), and the active protrusion is load-bearing (raises it from 0.17; 36% of enclosures need the force); inside-out invagination (Baum & Baum) is far more feasible (0.83). The coarse area+bending budget (0.61) and the 2D passive-adhesion CPM (1.00) arms overstated classical engulfment. Next fidelity rung: a triangulated-mesh run (pbg-mem3dg).
